title: Annotatio IV §.XXI: Bucer, Zwingli, Tigurines — speech and thing easily reconciled even with Luther
pass_a_gloss: further vindicated from these men’s prior §. XIII., from Bucer’s English Writings and the sentence of Zwingli and the old Tigurines — who as to manner of speaking equally and as to the Thing and truth more studiously and even to superstition emulated Berengar — meanwhile most easily to be reconciled even with Luther himself, as we have more largely and expressly proved in the preface to Bucer’s Eucharistic writings, soon to be restored to public light, parag. 15.
pass_b_english: Further vindication (their prior §.XIII): Bucer’s English writings and old Zwingli/Tigurine sentence — eager even to superstition after Berengar’s manner of speech and the Thing itself.
Yet they are most easily reconciled even with Luther — as Strimesius showed at large in the preface to Bucer’s Eucharistic writings (§15).
source_text: vindicata insuper ab horum priori §. XIII., ex Scriptis Buceri Anglicis, Zwinglii & Tigurinorum veterum sententiâ, quà modum loquendi æquè atque quà Rem & veritatem, Berengarium studiosius & ad superstitionem usque æmulantium, intereà cum ipso etiam Luthero quàm facillimè conciliandorum, quemadmodum id latius & ex professo evicimus in præfatione ad scripta Buceri Eucharistica, propediem in luci publica redonanda parag. 15.

choices.english: to be reconciled even with Luther himself
